batchName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476) - Medium Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)

questions.question: Which city at the head of the Adriatic did Attila raze when he invaded Italy in 452?
questions.explanation: Attila destroyed Aquileia. Disease, hunger and perhaps a papal embassy then persuaded him to turn back.
questions.sourceQuote: Attila returned in 452, invading Italy and razing Aquileia, a city at the head of the Adriatic.

questions.question: In a mocking story told by a later Greek historian, what did the emperor in Ravenna fear had perished when he heard 'Roma had perished'?
questions.explanation: The 6th-century story claimed the emperor was relieved to learn it was only the city, not his chicken named Roma. It mocked the emperor's indifference to Rome's fall.
questions.sourceQuote: He had feared for his favourite chicken, named Roma.

questions.question: Why was the loss of Africa to the Vandals such a blow to the Western Empire? (select all that apply)
options: It was the main source of Rome's grain
It supplied most of the army's horses
questions.explanation: Africa was rich, easy to defend and Rome's main grain supplier. To make up the loss, the government raised taxes on peasants who could pay no more.
questions.sourceQuote: Africa had been rich, easy to defend and the main source of Rome's grain.

questions.question: Roughly how many Vandals, Alans and others crossed the Rhine into Gaul in the early 400s?
questions.explanation: Perhaps 100,000 people crossed the Rhine into Gaul. This came on top of another Gothic horde ravaging northern Italy in 405 and 406.
questions.sourceQuote: Then perhaps 100,000 Vandals, Alans (nomadic horsemen from the steppe) and others crossed the Rhine (*Rhenus*) into Gaul.

questions.question: Which people became the main power in north-eastern Gaul as the empire shrank?
questions.explanation: The Franks took over north-eastern Gaul. Meanwhile Spain slipped into the hands of Sueves, Vandals and local strongmen.
questions.sourceQuote: Spain slipped into the hands of the Sueves, another Germanic people, the Vandals and local strongmen, while the Franks became the main power in north-eastern Gaul.

questions.question: When the Goths were settled as foederati after their rebellion, what did that mean?
options: They were enslaved on imperial estates
They kept their own leaders and fought for Rome
They were shipped off to guard Britain
They were disarmed and scattered among cities
They became Roman citizens and paid taxes
questions.explanation: Foederati were allied peoples who kept their own leaders and fought for Rome in return. Rome settled the Goths this way because it could neither crush nor expel them.
questions.sourceQuote: Instead they were settled as allies (*foederati*), peoples who kept their own leaders and fought for Rome in return.

questions.question: What happened to the western emperor a year after he killed Aetius?
options: He abdicated in favour of his son
He died of plague in Ravenna
He was captured by the Vandals
He was murdered by Aetius's supporters
questions.explanation: Aetius's supporters killed the emperor in revenge. A rich senator who had encouraged both murders then seized the throne.
questions.sourceQuote: A year later Aetius's supporters murdered the emperor in revenge.

questions.question: What happened to the king of the Visigoths at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains?
options: He was killed in the battle
questions.explanation: The Visigothic king died in the fighting. Attila withdrew to his camp of wagons, and Aetius let him go home.
questions.sourceQuote: The Visigothic king was killed, and Attila withdrew to his camp of wagons.

questions.question: What did one pagan historian blame Christianity for after the sack of Rome?
questions.explanation: He argued Christianity had sapped the empire's old virtues. Other pagans said Rome had lost divine protection by abandoning the sacrifices.
questions.sourceQuote: One pagan historian blamed Christianity for sapping the empire's old virtues.

questions.question: After deposing the last western emperor, what did Odoacer do with the imperial regalia?
options: Sent them to the emperor in Constantinople
Melted them down to pay his troops
questions.explanation: Odoacer ruled Italy himself and sent the imperial regalia to the emperor in Constantinople.
questions.sourceQuote: Odoacer then ruled Italy himself and sent the imperial regalia to the emperor in Constantinople.
